This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Reggaeton (dembow)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Drum grooves](index.qmd#drums)

## The pattern

Kick on every beat, with the snare on the sixteenth before beats 2 and 4 and on the and of 2 and 4: a 3+3+2 in sixteenths, twice a bar. Despacito, One Dance.

It belongs in *Reggaeton* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the reggaeton style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-hhquarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Four on the floor

Kick on every beat, snare and clap on 2 and 4, and the open hi-hat on every off-beat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-dance.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four on the floor","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Reggaeton (dembow), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Kick on every beat; snare on the sixteenth before 2 and 4 and on the and of 2 and 4: 3+3+2 in sixteenths, twice a bar. Learn the snare against the kick slowly.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reggaeton (dembow)","opts":{"groove":"dembow"}},{"label":"Four on the floor (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 92 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

## In other styles
